problem: The merge de-duplicates overlapping parts per segment, not per word. When a sentence crosses a fixed (overlapped) cut, part A heard only its start and part B only its end. Keeping one of the two segments loses words, and keeping both duplicates the words in the 2 s overlap. The plan doc says the opposite: "words cut at the edge of one part are heard whole in the other, and the merge keeps each word from one part only".
failureScenario: Fixed cuts happen whenever no pause of at least 0.5 s is found in the last 35% of a part. activityThreshold is capped at -32 dB and hold is 0.5 s, so this is the case for mixed sound with continuous background audio (music or a video playing) above -32 dBFS. There is one cut every ~599 s for OpenAI and ~299 s for Gemini. Simulation of a 1000 s recording, words 'one'..'six' spoken 596-602 s around the cut at 599: part 0 returns 'one two three four' and part 1 returns 'three four five six'. mergeParts outputs '596-598 one two three four' and '598-601.9 three four five six', so 'three four' appears twice. With a shorter sentence the overlap is at least half the shorter segment: the equal-margin tie keeps part 0's truncated segment and drops the words after cut+1 s. The builder's own test codifies the loss: part 1 heard 'across the cut', but the expected output is ['across', 8.3, 9.5] and 'the cut' is dropped.
fix:
Make the word-level split in placePart (src/shared/captions/transcriptMerge.ts), so that every word is kept from exactly one part:

1. If a segment has words, keep only the words whose middle (w.start + w.end) / 2 is in [part.keepStart, part.keepEnd). The last part also keeps keepEnd itself.
2. If no words remain, drop the segment.
3. If some words were dropped, the segment crossed a fixed cut. Set its start to the first kept word's start and its end to the last kept word's end, and rebuild its text from the kept words' text joined by spaces (cleanCaptionText). Segments that kept all their words keep their original text, so their punctuation stays.

Pieces split this way no longer overlap, so the segment-level dedupe in mergeParts only acts on segments without words. For those (for example Gemini answers that omit words), keep today's whole-segment rule, since the text cannot be split.

Also:
- Update tests/transcriptMerge.test.ts so the overlap case has word timings and expects 'across' from part 0 plus 'the cut' from part 1, with no repeat and no loss.
- Add a case for a long straddling sentence (both segments longer than 4 s) that checks the words in the overlap appear only once.
- Optionally, in mergeParts' final pass, rebuild the text when the trimming at lines 68-70 drops words, so text and words never disagree.

return message.content.map((block) => (block.type === 'text' ? block.text : '')).join('')

If the code is ever switched to non-streaming, the partial is already omitted there, so joining all text is correct in both modes.

The error is classified as 'other', is not retried, and the user sees the raw SSE JSON. The build report says 529/overloaded is retried.

- `APIError.makeMessage` finds no top-level `body.message`, so it uses `JSON.stringify(body)` as the message.
- `anthropicFailure` (src/main/ai/anthropic.ts:33-34) returns `{status: undefined, code: 'overloaded_error', message: '<raw JSON>'}`.

- What breaks is the less frequent mid-stream case. The cost is lost paid work on multi-batch tasks, plus an error message that is ugly but harmless.

if (status === 429) {

- A Gemini per-day 429 stays quota, through its `PerDay` quotaId in `code`.
- The e2e mock still gets quota, because its message has "PerDay" in it.

problem: The transcription temp folder ssw-transcribe-* in os.tmpdir() holds the whole recording decoded to 16 kHz PCM (~115 MB per hour, the user's voice in clear) plus MP3 parts. It is only removed in runJob's async finally. When the app quits mid-transcription, the will-quit handler only aborts and kills ffmpeg. The process exits before the async fs.rm runs, and nothing sweeps these folders later. Exports have a LeftoverLog and a startup sweep for their temp files; transcription has neither.
failureScenario: The user starts captions for a 1-hour recording and closes the app while it is transcribing (or the app crashes). %TEMP%\ssw-transcribe-XXXX\sound.pcm (~115 MB) stays behind for good. Each such quit leaves another copy.

Two changes, in src/main/ai/transcribe.ts and one register call.

1) Remove the folder on a normal quit. In transcribe.ts, give `Job` a mutable `tmp?: string`. `runJob` gets the job, or a setter, and records `tmp` right after `fs.mkdtemp`. In `stopAllTranscriptions()`, after `controller.abort()` and `processes.stopAll()`, call this for each job that has a `tmp`:

`removeSyncWithRetries(job.tmp, { rmSync: (f) => fs.rmSync(f, { recursive: true, force: true }) })`

Import it from `../exportCleanup`, together with the sync `fs` from `node:fs`. The default `rmSync` is not recursive, so the override is needed. The retries cover Windows still holding the handle of the just-killed ffmpeg.

2) Clean up after crashes, kills and failed deletes. Add a small startup sweep and call it from `registerAiIpc()`, for example:

`void sweepTranscribeTemp(app.getPath('temp'))`

The sweep reads the temp folder and, for each `ssw-transcribe-*` folder whose mtime is older than about 6 hours (longer than any job, since another running instance may own a younger one), runs `fs.promises.rm(dir, { recursive: true, force: true })` and ignores errors. Alternatively, put the PID in the prefix, for example `ssw-transcribe-<pid>-`, so the sweep can reuse `processAlive()` the way `sweepTempDir` does for GIF temps, and use a shorter age.

I tried to refute this and could not. I read the code at 48ed9a7.

How the folder is made and removed:
- `transcribe.ts:192` makes `ssw-transcribe-*` in `os.tmpdir()`.
- `decodeArgs` decodes the whole sound to `s16le` mono. `PCM_RATE` is `RATE*2`, so at 16 kHz that is 32,000 B/s, about 115 MB per hour.
- The folder is removed only in `runJob`'s `finally`, with `await fs.rm(tmp, {recursive, force, maxRetries: 3})`.
- The PCM stays on disk for the whole job, including every upload and provider round trip, so the window for a quit is long.

What happens on quit:
- `aiIpc.ts:99-102`'s `will-quit` handler calls `stopAllTranscriptions()`. That function does `controller.abort()` and `processes.stopAll()`, which is a `proc.kill('SIGKILL')` loop. Nothing is awaited.
- After that, `runJob` can only finish through async steps: the ffmpeg 'close' event or the fetch abort rejection, then the `finally`, then the threadpool `fs.rm`. With `maxRetries`, `fs.rm` also uses timers.
- Electron exits right after the `will-quit` handlers return, so none of that runs. The codebase says the same thing in its own comment on `removeSyncWithRetries`: "only for quitting, when nothing asynchronous runs any more".
- On Windows, the ffmpeg just killed with TerminateProcess can still hold `sound.pcm` for a moment, so even a prompt delete could fail.

Nothing else covers it:
- The only `before-quit` handler (`exportIpc.ts:308`) waits only for export cleanups, and only when an export is active.
- No window 'close' guard or renderer path cancels or waits for a transcription. Editor.tsx's `beforeunload` only flushes the project.
- `grep` for `ssw-transcribe` finds only the `mkdtemp`.
- `sweepTempDir` only matches `GIF_TEMP`, and `LeftoverLog` is only used for exports.
- So nothing removes these folders after a quit mid-job, and nothing does after a crash or kill either.

The scenario happens through the real UI: start Generate captions on a long recording, then close the window while it runs. `window-all-closed` leads to `app.quit`, then `will-quit`, and the folder stays behind. Each such quit leaves another copy, holding the user's voice unencrypted, in %TEMP%.

Why low: it is a disk and privacy leak in the temp folder. There is no data loss and nothing visible goes wrong.

problem: When a 'screen-only' segment sits directly next to a segment that put the camera in its own corner, the camera slides diagonally across the frame while it fades. `segmentCorner()` only keeps corners for 'default' and 'camera-large'. So the screen-only state's hidden bubble is placed by `layoutGeometry('screen-only', …, undefined)` at the project's corner, not where the camera was. Between back-to-back segments, `sceneLayout` interpolates from the cornered bubble to that hidden bubble. Bubble recordings produce back-to-back corner segments, so this happens as soon as one of them is changed to Screen only.
failureScenario: Default corner is bottom-right. The bubble was moved to top left at 10 s and to top right at 20 s, giving segments TL[10,20) and TR[20,30). In the editor the user selects the TR change (or uses the palette command 'Camera layout: screen only') to hide the camera from 20 s. Measured with tsx: at t=20.2 the camera box is at x=856, y=436 (the middle of a 1920×1080 frame) at 0.5 opacity, travelling from the top-left corner (x=43, y=43) to bottom right (x=1669, y=829). The same happens in reverse when a screen-only segment is followed directly by a cornered one. This shows in both preview and export.
fix:
Change only src/shared/engine/layout.ts (two small edits).

1) In `phase()`, give a 'screen-only' side the corner of the other side, so the hidden bubble fades where the camera was:

```ts
function phase(from: LayoutState, to: LayoutState, progress: number): LayoutPhase {
  const p: LayoutPhase = { from: from.layout, to: to.layout, progress }
  const fromCorner = from.layout === 'screen-only' ? to.corner : from.corner
  const toCorner = to.layout === 'screen-only' ? from.corner : to.corner
  if (fromCorner) p.fromCorner = fromCorner
  if (toCorner) p.toCorner = toCorner
  return p
}
```

2) In `layoutGeometry()`, let a passed corner place the hidden bubble:

```ts
const webcam = corner && (cornered(layout) || layout === 'screen-only') ? { ...project.webcam, corner } : project.webcam
```

Why this is safe:
- `sameState`/`segmentCorner` still decide whether a change animates, so the ramp logic is unchanged.
- A settled screen-only phase (`phase(to, to, 1)`) and the ramps to and from `DEFAULT_STATE` still have no corner, so they behave as today.

Add a test in tests/cameraLayouts.test.ts: back-to-back segments, default TL [10,20) then screen-only [20,30). At t=20.2 the camera rect centre should stay in the top-left quadrant. Add the same check for the reverse order.

problem: After Restart on the recording bar, the main window stays hidden on purpose: cancel(token, true) calls endRecordingUi(true), which skips main.show(), and also hides the toolbar. reasoning:
I confirmed the defect by reading the code at 48ed9a7. Restart was added in wave 4: the base 2144728 has no "restart" in controller.ts or recordingIpc.ts, and its endRecordingUi always called main.show().

How it happens:
1. The Restart button only appears while recording or paused (Toolbar.tsx:149, 234). Confirming sends the 'restart' command.
2. In controller.ts, finish('restart') then calls api.cancelRecording(token, true) (lines 151 or 167).
3. In main, cancel(token, true) runs discard(s), which sets active=null, then endRecordingUi(true). That hides the toolbar and skips main.show() (recordingIpc.ts:336-355). The main window stays hidden: setStatus 'countdown'/'recording' hid it (line 747-748).
4. runRecording (controller.ts:21-25) loops into recordOnce again, which calls api.prepareCapture. If that rejects, line 42 rethrows with no cleanup. No token exists yet, so cancelRecording is never called.
5. Home.record's catch (Home.tsx:640-645) only calls setError on the hidden window. Nothing in the renderer shows the main window.

Nothing in main shows it either. The only main.show() calls are in endRecordingUi(false), focusApp (second instance) and regionWindow. There is no tray (grep finds none). Global hotkeys were unregistered in endRecordingUi. Failures after a token exists are handled: for example, an acquire() failure calls cancelRecording(token), which runs endRecordingUi(false) and shows main. So the gap is only prepare() failing after a restart.

Ways prepare() can fail after a restart:
- resolveSource can no longer find the source: "no longer available".
- createProjectDir or writeManifest fails (disk or permission problems with the projects folder).
- The region or display check fails.

The trigger is rarer than the claim says. If the recorded window is closed or its display unplugged while recording, the recording usually stops by itself first: onNativeEnded leads to stopAfterNativeEnd and 'stop', and in Chromium capture the track ending leads to finish('stop'). So the "window closed" case is a narrow race between confirming Restart and prepare(). Disk or permission failures, or a source that the source list no longer shows (for example, possibly a minimized window), are the more realistic triggers.

Impact when it happens: the main window is hidden (so not on the taskbar) and the recording bar is hidden, so the app looks gone and the error is never seen. No data is lost, because the take was discarded on purpose. Relaunching the app recovers it: second-instance calls focusApp, and since active is null it shows main. For those reasons I rate it low rather than medium.

In src/shared/captions/transcriptText.ts textPrompt, when targetLanguage matches /^[a-z]{2,3}(-[A-Za-z0-9]+)*$/, resolve it with `new Intl.DisplayNames(['en'], { type: 'language' }).of(code)` and write it as `into ${name} (language code "${code}")`.
